default.notes: Tourist visa required, applied for at a Venezuelan embassy or consulate. Many Venezuelan missions are closed or working with reduced services, so allow a long lead time and confirm before paying any fee.

groups.notes: Visa-free for tourism for up to 90 days with a confirmed onward ticket; the officer writes the days actually granted on the entry stamp, which is often fewer than 90.

Reported as visa-exempt for short tourist stays under a bilateral arrangement, but Venezuela's exemption lists are poorly published and change with political circumstances — confirm with a Venezuelan consulate before booking.

VE.notes: Home country — no entry requirements for Venezuelan citizens.

US.notes: A visa is required, and it is hard to obtain: Venezuelan consulates in the United States have been closed since 2019, so applications must go through a Venezuelan consulate in a third country. The US embassy in Caracas is not operating and the US government advises against all travel to Venezuela — there is no US consular assistance available inside the country.

IL.notes: A visa is required and Venezuela has had no diplomatic relations with Israel since 2009, so there is no Venezuelan mission in Israel — any application has to be made through a Venezuelan consulate in a third country.

CN.notes: A visa is required for ordinary Chinese passports despite the close bilateral relationship; apply at the Venezuelan embassy in Beijing.
